eips.title: Bump nonce of zero-nonce storage accounts
eips.summary: Discussed whether to add it to Glamsterdam or defer to Hegota; decided not to add to Glamsterdam, will scope for Hegota.

moments.context: Ansgar raised EIP-8253 as a topic from ACDT, noting it bumps nonces of zero-nonce storage accounts and could potentially be added last-minute to Glamsterdam.
Jochem explained EIP-8253 replaces EIP-7610, is mainnet-only, and proposed adding it to Glamsterdam or immediately SFI-ing it for Hegota.
Toni said most clients were against adding it to Glamsterdam on ACDT, citing the BAL interaction and lack of testnet coverage, recommending it for Hegota instead.
Jochem confirmed Hegota is fine and requested it be SFI'd for Hegota to end the discussion.
Ansgar noted 8253 is on the Hegota priority list with one of the highest average client rankings, deferring the formal status decision to the Hegota scoping block.

eips.title: Revert creation in case of non-empty storage
eips.summary: Confirmed as DFI'd from Glamsterdam due to discovered problems; EIP-8253 replaces it for Hegota.

moments.context: Jochem said EIP-8253 will replace EIP-7610 for Hegota.
Ansgar asked if 7610 stays in Glamsterdam; Jochem clarified it was DFI'd after problems were found, despite having been SFI'd earlier.

eips.title: Call and Return Opcodes for the EVM
eips.summary: Decision delayed to next call; Greg Colvin championed it passionately, and clients agreed to wait for compiler team input before deciding.

moments.context: Ansgar identified EIP-7979 call and return opcodes as a borderline DFI candidate at 1.2 rating.
Jochem argued EVM-only EIPs have a blind spot in client rankings and asked not to DFI 7979 today to reflect on how to ship EVM EIPs.
Greg Colvin made an impassioned plea that EVM is the only smart contract VM without calls and returns, the implementation is simple and tested, and he has championed it for years.
Ansgar confirmed no DFI or CFI decision on 7979 today; chat supported delaying until compiler teams like Solidity can weigh in.

eips.title: Linear, Page-Based Memory Costing
eips.summary: DFI'd for Hegota after Charles presented its merits but no client team was willing to prioritize it; Ben Adams and Nethermind were sympathetic but not enough.

moments.context: Ansgar identified EIP-7923 linear page-based memory costing as a borderline DFI candidate at 1.3 rating.
Charles argued 7923 provides a modern virtual memory model, enables heap and stack for compilers, changes only the gas model with no new opcodes.
Ben Adams said the current EVM memory model is crazy and he is quite supportive.
Nethermind confirmed it is B tier (nice to have, not priority); ethrex still voted DFI.
Ansgar called for final opinions; lightclient said DFI, and Ansgar confirmed DFI decision for 7923.

eips.title: Reserve `EXTENSION (0xae)` opcode
eips.summary: Decision delayed to next call; Ansgar asked for L2 and alt-L1 demand signals before then, otherwise default is DFI.

moments.context: Ansgar identified EIP-8163 reserve EXTENSION opcode as a borderline DFI candidate.
Ansgar voiced support for delaying the decision to give other EVM chains time to show interest.
Piotr argued the EIP is a no-op but enables research on alternative EVMs; without commitment, chains cannot pursue extension-based designs.
Ansgar said the champion must produce a list of L2s expressing interest by next call or the default outcome is DFI.

eips.title: Subroutines and Static Jumps for the EVM

moments.context: Jochem mentioned Greg had also made EIP-615 and has been working for years to get these features into the EVM.

eips.title: In-mempool signature and proof aggregation

Csaba confirmed in chat that there is work on aggregation via EIP-8288 and he is doing simulations.

eips.title: Batch priority fees at end of block
eips.summary: DFI'd for Hegota; Nethermind liked it for builder optimization but other teams saw too much complexity for the benefit.

moments.context: Ansgar raised EIP-8115 batch priority fees at end of block as a DFI candidate at 1.2 rating.
Nethermind said they really like it for parallel block building optimization, considering it technical debt cleanup.
Marius from Geth said it adds a lot of outer-EVM complexity and implications around consensus rules, not worth it.
Nethermind confirmed it is not a hill they would die on; Ansgar made the DFI decision.

eips.title: EVMification
eips.summary: DFI'd for Hegota; seen as interesting for future zkEVM but premature now, pending EVM bytecode competition results.

moments.context: Ansgar raised EIP-8200 EVMification as a DFI candidate; ethrex had the only positive rating.
Ben Adams said it is interesting but too early given the ongoing precompile-replacement bytecode competition.
Justin Florentine from Besu flagged the risk of reverting native implementations if gas costs cannot be statically determined.
Ethrex argued it reduces prover attack vectors and removes complexity for zkEVM teams but accepted the DFI given other teams' positions.
Ansgar confirmed DFI for EIP-8200 for Hegota, noting likely revisit in future forks.

eips.title: Delayed State Root
eips.summary: DFI'd for Hegota; Besu's Karim argued it helps performance by removing state root from the hot path, but others saw insufficient benefit.

moments.context: Ansgar raised EIP-7862 delayed state root as a DFI candidate; Besu was the only client with a positive rating.
Karim from Besu explained state root computation takes significant time and this EIP would allow computing it between blocks.
Nethermind's Łukasz countered that state root is not a big problem for them, especially post-BAL with parallel computation, and the ecosystem repercussions should be avoided.
Ansgar confirmed DFI decision for 7862, noting possible revisit with binary trees or if Glamsterdam reveals unexpected load.

eips.title: Normalized state gas limit
eips.summary: Decision delayed; despite very low client ratings, Maria and Anders argued it may be needed post-Glamsterdam if gas demand is unbalanced.

moments.context: Ansgar raised EIP-8372 normalized state gas limit as a DFI candidate with one of the lowest client ratings overall.
Maria asked to delay the decision on both 8372 and 8368 until after Glamsterdam launches so demand effects can be observed.
Anders argued both should be CFI'd now since we may need to rebalance state and execution gas post-Glamsterdam.
Marius from Geth said they chose the simpler 8368 but acknowledged the choice was made without sufficient information; agreed to give it more time.
Ansgar confirmed no DFI for 8372 today; it will be discussed alongside 8368 at a later call.

eips.title: CPSB Recalibration for New Gas Limit
eips.summary: Has solid client support as the simpler recalibration option; will be discussed for CFI next call alongside EIP-8372.

moments.context: Maria asked for both 8368 and 8372 decisions to be delayed until after Glamsterdam ships.
Ansgar noted 8368 CPSB recalibration has a lot of support and is a likely CFI candidate.
Marius explained Geth chose 8368 as the simpler-worded option; Dragan said Reth made the same choice.

eips.title: State Creation Gas Cost Increase
eips.summary: Referenced as the Glamsterdam EIP whose real-world demand effects need to be observed before deciding on 8372 and 8368.

moments.context: Maria said the decision on 8372 and 8368 should wait until after Glamsterdam ships so demand reaction to EIP-8037 can be observed.

eips.title: SSZ execution blocks
eips.summary: DFI'd for Hegota; Geth cited high blast radius and low user benefit, Reth said the current API works and is not broken.

moments.context: Ansgar raised EIP-7807 SSZ execution blocks as a DFI candidate with relatively unanimous rejection; ethrex had the only positive rating.
Marius said benefit is very low for users but impact is very high, everything reading headers/blocks must change; blast radius is crazy.
Dragan said the current API works, is not a bottleneck, and should only be revisited when something breaks.
Ansgar confirmed DFI decision for EIP-7807 SSZ execution blocks.

eips.title: Trustless log and transaction index
eips.summary: Decision delayed; Geth's lightclient argued it enables trustless log range queries not possible today, Besu agreed to engage further before next call.

moments.context: Ansgar raised EIP-8304 trustless log and transaction index; Geth is the only client with a positive rating.
Zsolt (author) said the EIP has positive feedback from those who care about it, enables on-chain provability and L2 communication, and there is never a perfect time.
Lightclient argued this enables trustless RPC proofs about event range queries that cannot be done today, drawing a parallel to FOCIL and censorship resistance.
Besu's Justin Florentine agreed to accept a delay decision and asked the champion to explain why off-chain trusted solutions are insufficient.
Nethermind said they gave it B tier, have a contributor PR prototype, and are fine including it if others support it.
Ansgar confirmed delay decision for 8304; default is still DFI unless clients are convinced in the next two weeks.
